messages:
Sophie (PM): Heads-up — dropping a draft PRD + SLO thread for the 'Predictable Tail' initiative. Goal: make tail latency predictable for hosted chat/generation. Need acceptance criteria, edge-case list, and rollout plan.
Maya (Eng-ML): Quick q — does this cover chat + embeddings + batch-only endpoints or just interactive text gen?
Sophie (PM): Primary focus: interactive text gen / chat for now (streaming + non-streaming). Embeddings follow-up later.
Chris (SRE): Critical: define error budget & burn-rate triggers. Also need per-route p50/p95/p99 telemetry. If p99 spikes, what's rollback?
Alex (Product): Customer ask from a mid-market fintech — wants SLA for 99.95% uptime and p99 under 300ms for observed traffic. Is that realistic without Dedicated? :eyes:
Nikhil (Eng-Platform): For hosted, hitting p99 300ms at scale implies more reserved capacity (cost). Autoscaler + burst pool can help but we need cost guardrails.
Sophie (PM): Draft acceptance criteria (early):
```
Acceptance criteria:
- p99 latency <= 350ms for requests <= 1024 tokens (hosted chat) measured at edge across 1m windows
- p95 <= 120ms
- Monthly uptime >= 99.9% for the feature route
- Error budget <= 0.1% (production requests) monthly
- Graceful degradation: when capacity > 90%, route falls back to cached prefix or smaller model within 200ms extra
- Canary rollout with 1% -> 10% -> 50% steps, monitor burn rate
```
Maya (Eng-ML): Edge cases to call out: long contexts (>8k), tokenization variance, fallback model hallucination risk, quantized model quality drops. Need eval set + regression threshold.
Chris (SRE): Observability must include: per-request trace id, token-level timing, model-switch events, and per-canary burn-rate. Rollback triggers: "error budget burn rate > 3x for 15m" or p99 > 2x SLA for 10m.
Nikhil (Eng-Platform): Also add cost-impact alert: if projected monthly cost increase for served traffic > 15% then pause auto-scale to burst and notify finance.
Alex (Product): From customers: acceptance tests should include semantic-quality checks — no more than X% drop on eval prompts. We should define X (suggest 2-3%).
Maya (Eng-ML): I'll draft the RFC acceptance tests: perf benchmarks + quality regressions. Plan: run A/B on historical prompts, measure latency and top-level quality metrics.
Sophie (PM): Rollout plan + launch criteria proposal:
- Dev sign-off + perf vetting in staging
- Canary: 1% for 24h (green) -> 10% for 48h (green) -> 50% smoke -> full
- Metrics gating: burn-rate <= 1.5x, p99 within 1.2x of target, quality regression <= 2%
- Post-launch 30d monitoring and formal SLA toggle for sales
Chris (SRE): Also need runbook snippets in PRD: how to force fallback, circuit-breaker commands, how to drain canary, and postmortem checklist.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started: canary-id=pt-20260307-01 -> 1% traffic.
Nikhil (Eng-Platform): Implementation notes: prefer async prefix caching + KV cache TTL tuned to 60s, and conservative batch windows to avoid tail amplification.
Alex (Product): Agree with acceptance + tests. Add: explicit customer opt-in for SLA (requires commitment + billing change).
Maya (Eng-ML): I can own the RFC write-up this week. Will include: SLO definitions, acceptance scripts, eval sets, known edge-cases, and a short QA checklist.
Sophie (PM): Thanks — can everyone add any missing edge-case lines in the thread by EOD? I'll fold into the PRD and tag for review. :thumbsup:
